title: The House among the idols
hookLine: the Ka'ba of Ibrahim, now surrounded by idols, and pilgrims still came

cards: Surah fifty-three names them, goddesses the Meccans honored. In the Mecca the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ would be born into, figures like these stand around a stone house in a dry valley.
And still, season after season, pilgrims come to walk around that house, circling it, calling out, leaving again for home. Who put the idols there? And who built the house before them, and for whom?
The Qur'an has an answer, and it isn't any of the figures standing there. Today: the House among the idols.

teach.b: The house is the Ka'ba, a stone building roughly the shape of a cube. Surah two remembers how it began, in Pickthall's translation: "And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House."

In surah twenty-two, Allah tells Ibrahim to purify the House for those who walk around it, stand, bow and prostrate. That was its first purpose. By the time of the Prophet's birth, the sirah says, it had filled up.

The three goddesses had their own shrines elsewhere in the region, but at the House itself the sirah places a god called Hubal, whose name, Sahih al-Bukhari remembers, Abu Sufyan called out at the battle of Uhud.

And Ibn Mas'ud reports, in al-Bukhari, that on the day the Prophet entered Mecca years later, idols stood all around the House, three hundred and sixty in his telling, and the Prophet struck them with a stick, reciting a verse that Pickthall renders: "Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away."
That is the end of this story. Today is the cluttered middle. Even then, the House had not quite forgotten.
Sahih Muslim preserves the cry the Meccans called out as they circled: here I am, O Lord, here I am, You have no partner.
And then they added: except a partner who is Yours, whom You own, along with all he owns.
The report says that when they reached no partner, the Prophet would say: stop there, enough.

Pilgrims at the Hajj still call out a cry like it, the talbiyah, and in the version the Prophet taught, You have no partner stands with nothing added. Under the idols, the foundations were still Ibrahim's.

how: Pilgrims at the Hajj and the 'umrah call out the talbiyah, the pilgrim's cry declaring that God has no partner, as they travel to and circle the Ka'ba.

games.q: you're beside the Prophet ﷺ as Meccans circle the House calling out: You have no partner... and they're about to add their exception. what does he say?
games.why: Sahih Muslim reports he would say: stop there. the cry was right up to the exception.

practice: Picture an old house with things piled on things, and walk through it until you find one wall that was there before the clutter; in your mind, put your hand flat against it.
If you pray, you can ask Allah to show you what has piled up around what matters in your own life; if you don't, simply notice what the clutter is covering.

wordCard.voice: Ka'ba. The stone house raised for one God, crowded with idols before the Prophet ﷺ, and still walked around by pilgrims today. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Ka'ba, the House at Mecca.
